exposure: Timing of CM-I diagnosis (before vs after childbirth)
cohort: The study included 866 patients with Chiari malformation type I and 11,000 normal controls, identified from insurance claims data for childbirth admissions between 2004 and 2014.
finding: A diagnosis of Chiari malformation type I (CM-I) prior to delivery is associated with a higher rate of C-section and a lower rate of epidural analgesia, despite similar rates of serious maternal morbidity compared to normal controls.
mod_finding: A diagnosis of Chiari malformation type I prior to delivery is associated with a higher rate of C-section.
